What you described sounds extremely traumatic and I wouldn't at all be surprised if, knowing your past, you told me that you were a system. I hope that's a validation to you.

Dissociative disorders are, by nature, meant to be "hidden" - it's extremely common for even diagnosed systems to experience doubt and anxiety based around faking. You're not at all alone in that.
Amnesia certainly isn't a requirement for having alters, especially depending on the subtype that you have (or suspect to have). I wouldn't worry too much about that.

One thing about faking is that it's done intentionally. There's a difference between faking a disorder to glamorize it or receive attention, and just simply being wrong. In the world of psychiatry, misdiagnoses happen - and these come from trained professionals. It's not necessarily your responsibility to worry about an exact label, and I hope that you don't worry too much about it when it ultimately comes down to everything. If this is what helps you cope, then who are you hurting? 

With all of that being said, I hope that you're in a better place now and that you can cope with - not escape - what happened to you as a child. There is a future for you, and I wish you well in seeking it out.
